in_arabic.name: مجدد
in_arabic.meaning: من يعيد الإحياء والنشوء الجديد في الدين الإسلامي
in_arabic.long_meaning: المجدد هو الشخص الذي يعيد الإحياء والنشوء الجديد في الدين الإسلامي، ويجدد الهمة والنشاط في نفوس المسلمين، ويقوم بتفسير وتوضيح الدين الإسلامي بطريقة جديدة ومحدثة، ويعتبر المجدد من الشخصيات المهمة في التاريخ الإسلامي، حيث يسهم في تجديد الدين الإسلامي وإعادة إحيائه.

in_urdu.name: مجدد
in_urdu.meaning: جو شخص اسلام کی بحالی اور نئی زندگی کا سبب بنتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: مجدد وہ شخص ہوتا ہے جو اسلام کی بحالی اور نئی زندگی کا سبب بنتا ہے، اور مسلمانوں کے دلوں میں نئی ہمت اور سرگرمی کو جنم دیتا ہے، اور اسلام کے تعلیمات کو ایک نئی اور جدید انداز میں پیش کرتا ہے، اور اس کا تعلق اسلامی تاریخ میں ایک اہم شخصیت کے طور پر دیکھا جاتا ہے، جو اسلام کی تجدید اور بحالی کا کام کرتا ہے.

in_hindi.name: मुजद्दिद
in_hindi.meaning: जो व्यक्ति इस्लाम की पुनर्स्थापना और नए जीवन का कारण बनता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुजद्दिद वह व्यक्ति होता है जो इस्लाम की पुनर्स्थापना और नए जीवन का कारण बनता है, और मुसलमानों के दिलों में नई हिम्मत और सक्रियता को जन्म देता है, और इस्लाम की शिक्षाओं को एक नए और आधुनिक तरीके से प्रस्तुत करता है, और इसे इस्लामी इतिहास में एक महत्वपूर्ण व्यक्ति के रूप में देखा जाता है, जो इस्लाम की नवीनीकरण और पुनर्स्थापना का काम करता है।

in_pashto.name: مجدد
in_pashto.meaning: چې د اسلام د بیا رغونې او نوي ژوند سبب ګرځي
in_pashto.long_meaning: مجدد هغه څوک دی چې د اسلام د بیا رغونې او نوي ژوند سبب ګرځي، او د مسلمانانو په زړونو کې نوې هڅې او فعاليت رامینځته کوي، او د اسلام تعليمات په نوې او اوسني ډول وړاندې کوي، او د اسلامي تاريخ په منځ کې د يو مهم شخص په توګه ليدل کيږي، چي د اسلام د تجديد او بیا رغونې کار کوي.

in_english.name: Mujaddid
in_english.meaning: One who brings about renewal and revival in Islam
in_english.long_meaning: Mujaddid refers to a person who brings about renewal and revival in Islam, rejuvenating the faith and spirit of Muslims. Etymologically derived from the Arabic root 'j-d-d' which means 'to renew', the term Mujaddid holds significant importance in Islamic history and tradition. Throughout Islamic history, Mujaddids have played crucial roles in reviving and reinterpreting Islamic teachings, often marking significant periods of reform and spiritual rejuvenation.

pronunciation.urdu: مجدد کا تلفظ ہے م ج د د
pronunciation.pashto: مجدد تلفظ د مج د د

data.cultural_impact: The title "Mujaddid" holds immense historical importance as it is given to those Islamic scholars and leaders who revitalize and rejuvenate the teachings and practices of Islam. This title is not only associated with the classical period of Islamic history but continues to be relevant even in the modern world. During times of religious decline and social turmoil, the Mujaddids serve as beacons of guidance, illuminating the path to righteousness for the global Muslim community. Their contributions often lead to significant social, political, and educational reforms, contributing to the cultural richness and diversity of Islamic civilization.
data.spiritual_significance: The title "Mujaddid" carries immense spiritual significance as it represents an individual's commitment to the spread of divine knowledge and the revival of faith in the Muslim world. It is a reminder of the Prophet Muhammad's injunction "to enjoin good and forbid evil." For a person to be recognized as a Mujaddid underscores their piety and dedication to the teachings of the Prophet and the principles of the Quran and the Sunnah. As spiritual beings, they strive to walk in the footsteps of the Prophets and act as intermediaries between God and the people. Their lives exemplify the ideal of continuous self-improvement and standing up for justice and virtue within their communities and broader society. In essence, the title "Mujaddid" embodies the eternal quest for righteous living, bringing people closer to God and inviting them towards the divine abundance.

historical_references.reference: Al-Mujaddid Al-Faqih As-Sayyid Abdul-Hasan Al-Hilli (1252-1311 CE). Also known as Allamah Hilli, he was a prominent Shia scholar, jurist, and theologian of the Islamic golden age in Iraq. He is considered to be the 'Revivifier' or 'Renewer' (Mujaddid) of the Shia faith in the sixth Islamic century.
historical_references.context: The Islamic golden age in Iraq was a period of cultural, economic, and scientific flourishing. Al-Mujaddid Al-Faqih contributed significantly to Shia jurisprudence, theology, and philosophy.

historical_references.reference: Shah Waliullah Dahlawi (1703-1762 CE). He was a prominent Islamic scholar, theologian, and reformer from the Indian subcontinent. He is considered to be the 'Revivifier' or 'Renewer' (Mujaddid) of the Islamic faith in the 11th Islamic century (18th century AD).
historical_references.context: The Islamic world was experiencing a crisis due to various factors including political instability, intellectual stagnation, and religious decay. Shah Waliullah led the effort to revive and reform the Islamic faith, emphasizing the importance of religious scholarship, moral values, and social justice.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern usage, the Islamic title 'Mujaddid' (Arabic: مجدد, meaning 'renewer' or 'reviver') is given to a person who is believed to have revived or rejuvenated Islamic knowledge, practices, or thought in a particular period of time. This title has gained significance in various Islamic contexts through scholarship, politics, and culture. Scholars who have made significant contributions to Islamic knowledge or thought in a particular era are often referred to as Mujaddid. Politically, leaders who have worked towards the revival and renewal of Islamic principles in their societies have also been given this title. Culturally, artists, writers, and thinkers who have revived or rejuvenated Islamic art, literature, or philosophy are also referred to as Mujaddid.

name_in_real_life.story: A successful entrepreneur named Maryam Mujaddid in Cairo, Egypt attributes much of their success to the blessing of their name Mujaddid, which means "Reviver". They believe their name has shaped their identity and guided them through life.

It is a title given to individuals who significantly contribute to the spiritual and moral uplift of the Muslim community.
